abstract: Membrane progesterone receptors (mPRs) mediate rapid hormone responses, yet how they engage effectors remains poorly understood. Here, we reveal a spatially regulated partnership between mPRs and the lipid hydrolase ABHD2 that provides a mechanistic basis for the early steps of non-genomic progesterone signaling in mammalian cells. Agonist stimulation promotes mPR-dependent accumulation of predominantly intracellular ABHD2 at the plasma membrane and enhances its association with mPRs. Although human ABHD2 binds progesterone, its phospholipase A2 activity requires partnership with mPRs and an intact catalytic site. ABHD2 deletion disrupts agonist-induced metabolic signaling in hepatic and muscle cells and affects glucose homeostasis in obese mice. Together, these findings uncover a conserved receptor-hydrolase signaling mechanism in which spatially regulated association and receptor-dependent enzymatic activity emerge as defining features of non-genomic steroid signaling.
